name: object-with-function-invocation-using-self-keyword-3ef2bbabcc/object-self-function-invocation-negative-e.bal
spec_references: Module-level declarations: Class definition; Supports `object-field`, `method-defn` and `object-type-inclusion` members
Module-level declarations: Function definition; Supports [`required-params`], [`defaultable-params`], [`included-record-param`] and [`rest-param`] in the signature
Statements: Break; Continue; Call; If/else; While; Local variable declarations; Foreach
Statements / Foreach: Currently only supports range, list, map, string and XML subtypes, and iterable objects
Expressions: Method call; New expression; List constructor; Variable reference; Field access expression
Operators: Multiplicative ops `*`, `%`, `/`; Relational ops `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`; Equality ops `==`, `!=`, `===`, `!==`
reason: This negative case asserts rejection of using self in method or module-function calls before required object fields are definitely initialized, including branches, loops, continue/break and rest arguments. These are class initialization and type/definite-initialization checks within the supported class, invocation and statement grammar; no essential construct is excluded by the subset restrictions.
test_design_notes: The @error comments mark compile-time rejection expectations; execution of the non-progressing while loops is not asserted.
testSelfKeywordInvocationWithInvocationArg constructs Person5 instead of Person6, though Person6's initializer remains subject to compile-time checking.
